not_admin_title: This page is for the server's owner
not_admin_body: You are signed in as {name}, but managing the server itself is reserved for its owner. Your apps are still one click away.
error_session_expired: Your session has ended. Reload the page to sign in again.
error_unauthenticated: Your session has ended. Reload the page to sign in again.
error_csrf: The request was refused for safety. Reload the page and try again.
error_guard_login_only_way_in: You can't turn this off yet: Yundera Login is the only way to sign in to this server until you create a local account.
error_guard_support_last_way_in: You can't turn this off yet: with Yundera Login already off and no local account, the support key is the last way into this server.
error_already_claimed: This server already has an owner account. Reload the page.
error_login_off: Turn Yundera Login back on first: after the reset it is the only way back to the setup wizard.
error_invalid_username: Choose a username made of lowercase letters, digits, - or _, starting with a letter (32 characters at most).
error_invalid_password: Choose a password of at least 8 characters, on one line.
error_invalid_displayname: Enter a name of 64 characters at most.
error_invalid_schedule: That schedule isn't valid. Use 5 cron fields, like 0 3 * * *, or "disabled".
error_support_unavailable: We couldn't reach Yundera to check support access. Try again in a minute.
error_invalid_subject: Give your message a short subject, on one line.
error_invalid_message: Write a message (10,000 characters at most).
status_health_okRunning: A check is running now. The last one passed {at}.
status_health_firstRun: The first check is running now.
status_health_noRun: No check has run yet. The first one starts tonight.
status_health_failed: The last check ({at}) found problems in: {failed}.
status_health_stale: The last check ran {at}. It should run every night.
status_updates_on: Your server installs Yundera updates automatically.
status_updates_onChannel: Updates are on, following the {channel} channel.
status_updates_off: Automatic updates are off: security fixes no longer arrive.
status_updates_local: Updates are paused for testing (local mode).
status_connection_ok: Connected. Your server's Yundera credential is valid until {until}.
status_connection_expiring: Your server's Yundera credential expires {at}. It is usually renewed on its own.
status_connection_unknown: Couldn't read the connection to Yundera.
status_storage_high: {percent}% full: {avail} left. Time to tidy up.
status_storage_full: {percent}% full: only {avail} left. Apps may stop working.
status_storage_unknown: Measuring… (available a few minutes after a restart)
status_support_on: Yundera support may sign in to help you.
status_support_off: Yundera support can't sign in to this server.
status_issue_health_failed: The last health check found problems. Look at what failed — or send it to support in one click.
status_issue_health_stale: The nightly health check hasn't run for more than two days.
status_issue_updates_off: Automatic updates are off. Your server no longer receives security fixes.
status_issue_updates_local: Updates are paused in local (testing) mode. Switch back to the stable channel when you're done.
status_issue_connection_expired: Your server's connection to Yundera has expired. Contact support.
status_issue_connection_expiring: Your server's connection to Yundera expires soon. If it isn't renewed by itself, contact support.
status_issue_storage_full: Your server is almost out of space. Remove files or apps you no longer need.
status_issue_storage_high: Your server's storage is getting full.
overview_intro: This is the control room of your personal server: is it healthy, is it up to date, and where to find everything else.
explain_public_ip: Your server's number on the Internet. You normally never need it: your domain name above points to it. Support may ask for it.
overview_all_tools_hint: What each part of your server is for
reboot_intro: Like restarting a computer. Useful when something seems stuck. Your apps and files are kept; they are just unavailable for a few minutes.
reboot_confirm_body: Every app will be unavailable for a few minutes — usually 2 to 5 — and come back by itself.
reboot_confirm_safe: Nothing is deleted. This page will reload once the server is back.
reboot_waiting: Restarting… this page will come back by itself.
health_intro: Every night your server checks itself from top to bottom: that its services are running, that updates are applied, that backups are configured. It repairs what it can by itself. Here is the latest check.
health_truncated: Only the end of this check is in the log, so the count may be incomplete.
health_failed_help: Each step below could not complete. The text is what it reported — you don't need to understand it: sending it to support (Support page) is the quickest fix.
explain_schedule: Nightly is best: the check may restart services, and few people use their server in the middle of the night. Times are in your server's time zone.
schedule_cron_hint: Minute, hour, day, month, weekday. 0 3 * * * means every day at 03:00. Use "disabled" to stop it — not recommended.
log_intro: The full record of what the checks did. Useful for support, rarely for you.
features_intro: What Yundera does for your server, and what changes if you turn it off. Everything here is on by default: these switches are for people who want to run things themselves.
feature_guard_login: Yundera Login is the only way to sign in until this server has a local account.
feature_guard_support: With Yundera Login off and no local account, the support key is the last way in.
feature_login_what: Sign in to this server with your Yundera account. The same account opens every app installed here.
feature_login_cost: Turned off, only accounts created on this server can sign in, and a forgotten password is yours to recover — Yundera can no longer let you back in.
feature_login_warning: Everyone signing in with a Yundera account loses access immediately. Make sure you know the password of a local account first.
feature_support_what: Lets Yundera support connect to your server to repair what breaks inside it. The key is checked again every night so it can't get lost by accident.
feature_support_cost: Turned off, the key is removed now and doesn't come back, and support can no longer look at your server when something goes wrong.
feature_support_warning: The key is removed from your server now. If you later need help with something you can't reach — a broken login, an app that won't start — nobody will be able to get in and look.
feature_updates_what: Yundera keeps the platform up to date: the system that runs your apps, these settings pages, and the software they use.
feature_updates_cost: Turned off, your server stays as it is today and security fixes stop arriving. Your apps keep running. After months frozen, turning updates back on replays every change at once.
features_fixed_intro: These are part of how your server works today and can't be switched off yet.
feature_domain_what: Your server's address on the Internet and its security certificate. Every app you install is published under it.
feature_domain_cost: Not optional yet: sign-in pages need it, and bringing your own domain isn't possible yet.
feature_mail_what: Password-reset and notification emails — your server's and your apps' — are sent through Yundera's mail service.
feature_mail_cost: Not optional yet, and it comes with the domain. Using your own mail server isn't possible yet.
feature_sslip_what: A second way to reach your apps, based on your server's public address. Useful if the main domain can't be reached.
feature_sslip_cost: Not optional yet: many apps keep this address in their own settings.
feature_appupdates_what: Keeping the apps you installed up to date without being asked.
feature_appupdates_cost: Not built yet: your apps update only when you ask them to, from your apps page.
channel_intro: Where your server takes its updates from. Leave it on Stable unless support asks you to change it.
explain_channel: Stable gets updates once they have been tested on many servers. Preview gets them first, as soon as they are written — handy to try something new, at the risk of meeting a bug first.
channel_main_desc: The latest changes, before everyone else. May contain bugs.
channel_local_desc: Pauses downloads so hand-placed scripts can be tested. Not for everyday use.
channel_custom_desc: A specific address, given by support.
channel_frozen: Automatic updates are currently off (see above). Choosing a channel takes effect once they are back on.
channel_saved: Saved. A health check is starting to apply it.
rerun_intro: Takes your server back to the very first step, as if it were new: you will create the owner account again.
rerun_detail: Existing local accounts are disabled (a backup of them is kept), and everyone else signed in here is signed out. Your apps and files are not touched.
rerun_confirm_body: Every local account on this server will be disabled, and you will set up the owner account again. You stay signed in with Yundera Login to do it.
rerun_done: Done. The previous accounts were saved to {backup}.
rerun_sessions_warning: Other people signed in here could not all be signed out. They will be at their next sign-in.
support_intro: Something not working? Yundera support can look at your server with you. You decide whether they may sign in.
access_what: When this is on, Yundera support can open a secure technical session on your server to diagnose and repair it.
explain_ssh: This uses SSH, the standard secure way to administer a server remotely. Support signs in with its own key — like a key to your door that only Yundera holds, and that you can take back at any time with this switch.
access_privacy: Support only signs in to fix the problem you reported. Turn this off at any time: access ends immediately.
access_pending: Access is being set up — it will be in place within a minute, or at tonight's health check at the latest.
access_still_present: Support's key is still on the server; it is removed at the next health check.
access_own_keys: Want to sign in over SSH yourself?
report_intro: Describe what you were doing and what went wrong. We reply by email.
report_subject_placeholder: e.g. My photo app won't open
report_message_placeholder: What happened, since when, and what you already tried.
explain_log: The record of your server's health checks (the Health check page). It helps support find the cause quickly. It contains no files or passwords.
report_grant_access: Let support sign in to look (you can turn it off later on this page)
report_sent: Sent to {to}. We'll get back to you by email.
tools_intro: Your server is made of a few parts, each with its own page. Here is what each one is for — and when you would go there.
tools_maison_body: Your server's home page and app store: install, open, update and remove apps, and adjust their settings.
tools_maison_when: Go there every day — it's where your apps live.
tools_backups_short: Keep copies of your apps and files
tools_backups_intro: Two pages, two levels. Maison decides what is backed up and when; Kopia is the engine that stores the copies. Most people only ever need the first one.
tools_backups_maison_body: The simple way to protect your data.
tools_backups_maison_1: Choose where copies go and how often they are made
tools_backups_maison_2: See every backup of each app, with its date
tools_backups_maison_3: Put a whole app back as it was — useful after a bad update or a mistake
tools_backups_kopia_body: The engine that stores the copies, encrypted and without duplicates.
tools_backups_kopia_1: Browse every snapshot like a folder
tools_backups_kopia_2: Get back a single file instead of a whole app
tools_backups_kopia_3: Check the storage the copies use
tools_backups_analogy: Maison is the planner that decides what to keep and when; Kopia is the vault where it is kept. To restore an app, use Maison. To fish out one lost file, use Kopia.
tools_accounts_body: Who can sign in to your server: your account, the people you invite, passwords. Advanced users also manage SSH access there.
tools_accounts_when: Go there to add a family member, or change a password.
tools_network_body: How your server is reached from the Internet: its domain, its security certificates, email sending, and which app opens at your main address.
tools_network_when: Go there if an address doesn't work, or to choose your home page app.
tools_subscription_body: Your plan, invoices and payment method, on yundera.com.
onboarding_intro: Let's create the owner account: it's the account that manages this server, independently of Yundera. Choose a username and a password you will remember.
onboarding_username_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, - and _. It can't be changed later.
explain_password: This password protects your server even if Yundera Login is turned off one day. Write it down somewhere safe: Yundera doesn't know it and can't send it back to you.
onboarding_generated: Here is your password. Copy it now: it won't be shown again.
onboarding_ready_body: Your account {username} is created. A few things to know:
onboarding_next_apps: Your apps are in Maison: that's where you install and open them.
onboarding_next_here: This page watches over your server. Come back if something seems wrong.
onboarding_next_help: Stuck? The Support page lets you write to us in one click.
error_wrong_key: That password doesn't open your backups. Check it and try again — it's the one you chose when backups were first set up.
error_repository_exists: Backups already exist in your backup space. Reload the page to restore them or start over.
error_not_awaiting_secret: Your backups are no longer waiting for a password. Reload the page to see where they are.
error_too_short: Choose a backup password of at least 16 characters.
error_invalid_backup_password: The backup password must be on one line.
error_confirm_mismatch: Yundera refused to wipe the backup space: it doesn't match this server. Contact support.
error_rate_limited: You started over too many times today. Try again tomorrow, or contact support.
error_backup_failed: Your server couldn't complete this backup step. Try again in a minute; if it keeps failing, contact support.
error_unknown_action: This action isn't supported. Reload the page.
error_unknown_slide: This setup step doesn't exist. Reload the page.
error_skip_failed: Couldn't save your choice. It will simply come back sooner.
onboarding_skip_hint: Skipped steps come back in 3 days. Nothing stops you from using your server meanwhile.
onboarding_done_body: Your server is ready to use. A few things to know:
onboarding_done_skipped: You skipped a step: we'll remind you in 3 days.
account_login_keep: You will also be able to sign in with your Yundera account.
account_login_off_after: Yundera Login will be turned off as soon as your account is created. Only your local account will open this server.
account_login_on: You can sign in with your local account or with your Yundera account.
password_saved: I saved this password somewhere safe (a password manager, or on paper).
backup_intro: Every night your server can copy your apps and files to Yundera's backup storage, so a broken server or a mistake never costs you your data.
explain_backup: A backup is a copy of your data kept somewhere else. If your server breaks, or you delete something by mistake, you can get it back from the copy.
backup_ready_body: Backups run every night, encrypted with your password. You'll find them in Maison, under Settings → Backups.
backup_disabled: Backups are off: your server is not backed up. You can turn them back on here or in Maison at any time.
backup_not_yet: Your server is not backed up until you finish this step.
backup_choose_intro: Choose the password that encrypts your backups. Nobody can read them without it — not even Yundera.
explain_backup_password: Your backups are locked with this password before they leave your server. Yundera never sees it and cannot reset it: if you lose it, nobody can open your backups. Keep it in a password manager or on paper, away from this server.
backup_working: Working… this can take several minutes. Keep this page open.
backup_found: Backups from a previous server were found in your backup space.
backup_restore_desc: Reconnect to your previous backups, to keep them and get your files back.
backup_restart_desc: Delete the old backups and choose a new password. Only if you lost the old one or don't need those files.
backup_old_password_hint: The password chosen when backups were first set up (or the one Yundera emailed you then).
backup_restart_warning: Every backup in the space is deleted for good. Files that only exist in those backups are lost.
backup_unavailable: Backups can't be set up on this server right now.
backup_unavailable_body: This isn't something you did wrong. Skip this step for now and let us know: we'll fix it on our side.
error_backup_busy: Another backup step is still running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
error_no_backup_space: Yundera found no backup space for this server. Contact support.
error_unreachable: Your server couldn't reach Yundera. Check again in a minute.
error_reset_busy: Your backup space is already being emptied. Wait a few minutes, then check again.
error_backup_disabled: Backups are off. Turn them on first.
